t: This is the statue of Sir Wilfrid Lawson in Victoria Embankment Gardens, installed on the twentieth of July 1909. Lawson was a temperance campaigner and radical Liberal politician who sat in the House of Commons for many years and was recognised as its leading humourist. The sculptor was David McGill. The monument originally had allegorical figures of Charity, Fortitude, Peace and Temperance, but they were stolen in 1979.
